did_you_know.text: Did you know? The angel of the Lord went up from Gilgal to the place called Bochim and reminded Israel that the Lord had brought them out of Egypt and into the land, in keeping with his promise to their ancestors.

Did you know? The angel of the Lord’s rebuke focused on two violations by Israel: making a covenant with the inhabitants of the land and failing to tear down their altars, contrary to the Lord’s command.
Did you know? The people responded to the angel’s words by weeping loudly—all the Israelites wept. However, the following verses show that their weeping did not prevent the problem from continuing.
Did you know? The place was called Bochim because of the people’s weeping, and there the Israelites offered sacrifices to the Lord.
Did you know? The Israelites served the Lord throughout the days of Joshua and throughout the days of the elders who lived after him and had seen all the great things the Lord had done for Israel.
Did you know? Joshua son of Nun died at the age of 110, and Scripture also calls him “the servant of the Lord.”
Did you know? After Joshua and that entire generation had died, a new generation arose. It did not know the Lord or the deeds he had done for Israel.
Did you know? The beginning of the decline described in the chapter was doing evil in the sight of the Lord and worshiping the Baals.
Did you know? In response to Israel’s distress, the Lord raised up judges whose role, as described here, was to save the people from their raiders and enemies.

Did you know? The nations Joshua left in the land were not merely a historical backdrop: according to the chapter, their presence was connected with testing whether Israel would keep the way of the Lord.
